components.note: 亻 (person) — a person falling over; marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做.
到 (dào) gives the sound: 倒 is dǎo (fall) or dào (upside down).

example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn shuāidǎo le.
example.english: He fell over by accident.
example.fact: 倒 has two readings: dǎo ('to fall, to collapse', as in 摔倒) and dào ('to pour, upside down', as in 倒水). Many learners need the context to pick the right reading: 倒了 (fell) vs. 倒茶 (pour tea).

examples.hanzi: 台风来了，很多树都倒了。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng lái le, hěn duō shù dōu dǎo le.
examples.english: A typhoon came and many trees fell.
He collapsed from exhaustion last night.

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.
釆 (distinguish) — sorting things out: 释 is to untangle and explain.
圣 stands in for 睪 in the traditional 釋; the same part is in 译 yì, 泽 zé and 择 zé.

example.hanzi: 请你解释一下这个词的意思。
example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ jiěshì yíxià zhège cí de yìsi.
example.english: Please explain the meaning of this word.
example.fact: 解 alone already carries the sense "to untie, to loosen" (as in 解开, "to undo a knot"), and 解释 extends that image figuratively — "untying" a confusing idea into something clear — the same root 解 that appears in 解决 (also in this batch), Mandarin’s verb for "resolving" a problem.

examples.hanzi: 我来向你解释这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái xiàng nǐ jiěshì zhège wèntí.
examples.english: Let me explain this problem to you.
His explanation is very clear.

components.note: 離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
example.english: My home is close to school.
example.fact: 离 is the word for distance: A 离 B 很远 / 很近 means A is far from or near to B. It also means to leave or separate, as in 离开 (leave) and 离婚 (divorce), and is used in 离不开 (can't do without).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā lí gōngsī yuǎn bu yuǎn?
examples.english: Is your home far from the office?

examples.pinyin: Lí kāichē hái yǒu shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: There are ten minutes left before the departure.

components.note: 彳 (step, walk) — 彳 is the left-step radical, as in 行, 径, 德; 往 is going toward.
王 (wáng) — near sound — 往 is wǎng, same syllable with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Qǐng wǎng qián zǒu.
example.english: Please walk forward.
example.fact: 往 is a preposition meaning 'towards' and is used with directions: 往左 (to the left), 往前 (forward), 往南 (south). It also forms 往往 ('often, frequently') and 以往 (in the past).

examples.hanzi: 你往前走一百米就到了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wǎng qián zǒu yìbǎi mǐ jiù dào le.
examples.english: Walk straight ahead a hundred meters and you're there.

examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē kāi wǎng jīchǎng.
examples.english: This bus goes to the airport.

components.note: 萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu yí wàn gè rén.
example.english: There are ten thousand people here.
example.fact: 万 is the unit of ten thousand, which makes Chinese big numbers different from English: 十万 is 'one hundred thousand', 一百万 is 'a million'. It also means 'extremely' in 万分 and 万一 ('in case').

examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng qìchē yào shí wàn kuài.
examples.english: This car costs a hundred thousand yuan.
What if it rains?

meanings: variant of 聯繫|联系[lian2 xi4]

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and joining, as in 听, 聪, 闻: 联 first meant ears joined, so to link. The part 关 stands in for the traditional shape.
糸 (silk thread; 纟 on the left) — ties and connections, as in 红, 给, 经. 系 is a link or relation.

example.pinyin: Yǒushì qǐng suíshí liánxì wǒ.
example.english: If anything comes up, please contact me anytime.
example.fact: 联系 works equally well as a verb ("to get in touch with someone," 联系我) and a noun ("a connection, a relationship," 保持联系, "keep in touch") with no change in form — common enough in Mandarin that it’s worth checking both the verb and noun gloss whenever a new two-character word like this shows up.

examples.english: Please keep in touch.

examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn shì méiyǒu liánxì.
examples.english: These two things aren't related.

components.note: 氵 (water radical) — 派 first meant a stream branching off a river, which grew into branch, faction and to send out.

example.pinyin: Gōngsī pài tā qù Běijīng.
example.english: The company is sending him to Beijing.
example.fact: 派 is a verb for assigning or dispatching someone, as in 派人 and 派出所 (local police station). It also means a faction, school or style, as in 学派, 党派 and 派对 (party, borrowed from English).

examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn pài wǒ qù Shànghǎi chūchāi.
examples.english: The boss is sending me to Shanghai on a business trip.

examples.hanzi: 学校派了一位老师来接你。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào pàile yí wèi lǎoshī lái jiē nǐ.
examples.english: The school sent a teacher to pick you up.

components.note: 关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ mén guānshang.
example.english: Please close the door.
example.fact: 关 means to close or turn off: 关门, 关灯 (turn off the light), 关机 (shut down). It also means a customs checkpoint (海关) and is the word in 关系 (relationship) and 关心 (care about).

examples.pinyin: Chūmén qián bié wàngle guān dēng.
examples.english: Don't forget to turn off the lights before leaving.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ diànnǎo guān le ba.
examples.english: Shut down the computer.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 这张照片可以证明他当时在场。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn kěyǐ zhèngmíng tā dāngshí zàichǎng.
example.english: This photo can prove that he was present at the time.
example.fact: 证明 functions as both the verb "to prove" and the noun "a certificate, proof document" (身份证明, "identity certificate") — English keeps a similar verb/noun split ("to prove" vs. "proof"), but 证明 additionally covers the concrete bureaucratic sense of an official paper you must submit, with no single-word English equivalent.

examples.english: Do you need any kind of certificate?

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng zhèngmíng zìjǐ shì duì de.
examples.english: He wants to prove he's right.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — wrapping 勹 around 口: a mouth-sized group of words, so a sentence, as in 一句话 one sentence.

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài shuō yí jù.
example.english: Please say one more sentence.
example.fact: 句 is both the word for a sentence and its measure word: 一句话 (one sentence), 句子 (sentence), 句号 (period). Note that the ‘gōu’ reading of this character is a rare variant.

examples.pinyin: Zhège jùzi wǒ bú tài dǒng.
examples.english: I don't quite understand this sentence.

examples.hanzi: 他只说了一句话就走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐ shuōle yí jù huà jiù zǒu le.
examples.english: He said just one sentence and left.

components.note: 二 (two) — the top and bottom bars. Dictionary story: five elements between heaven and earth, with a cross in the middle; memory aid, not firmly attested.

example.pinyin: Tā jīnnián wǔ suì.
example.english: He is five years old.
example.fact: 五 is also in 五一 (May 1st, Labour Day) and in classical lists like 五行 (the five elements). It is also used for 'several' loosely, as in 五花八门 ('all kinds of').

examples.english: We get off work at five.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu wǔ běn shū.
examples.english: There are five books on the table.

meanings: life (as the characteristic of living beings)

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.

example.hanzi: 每一个生命都值得尊重。
example.pinyin: Měi yí gè shēngmìng dōu zhídé zūnzhòng.
example.english: Every life deserves respect.
example.fact: 生命 names life as a biological or philosophical force — "life" in the abstract, as something precious or at risk — while the similar-looking 生活 means "life" in the sense of daily living and lifestyle; mixing the two up is a common learner slip since English "life" covers both.

examples.english: Life is more important than money.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo gǒu de shēngmìng hěn duǎn.
examples.english: This puppy's life is short.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yǒudiǎn lèi.
example.english: I’m a little tired today.
example.fact: 有点 sits directly before an adjective to soften it (有点累, "a bit tired"; 有点贵, "a bit pricey") and tends to modify something negative or undesirable far more often than something positive — native speakers reach for 有点丑 ("a bit ugly") much more readily than 有点好看 ("a bit good-looking"), an asymmetry that trips up learners who treat 有点 as a neutral intensifier.

examples.english: This soup is a bit salty.
I'm a little homesick.

components.note: 告 (gào) — loose hint — 靠 is kào; 告 also sounds out 造 zào and 酷 kù.
非 (not) — two wings pointing away from each other, so back to back; as a memory aid, 靠 is leaning your back on something.

example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ kào wǒ.
example.english: You can rely on me.
example.fact: 靠 means to lean on or depend on: 靠窗 (by the window), 靠自己 (rely on oneself), 靠谱 (reliable, colloquial). It also means to be near to, as in 靠近.

examples.english: He is standing leaning against the wall.

examples.hanzi: 这件事你不能只靠别人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ bù néng zhǐ kào biérén.
examples.english: On this matter you can't just rely on others.

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.
冫 (ice) — here the ice form of 氵 (water): 决 first meant to break a dam, so a decisive break.
夬 (guài) is a loose sound clue for jué; 夬 also sounds out 快 kuài and 块 kuài.

example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí hěn nán jiějué.
example.english: This problem is very hard to solve.
example.fact: 解决 implies actually resolving a problem down to nothing left to deal with, in contrast to 处理 (also in this batch), which just means attending to or handling something — you can 处理 a complaint without truly 解决-ing the underlying issue, a distinction useful for calibrating how thoroughly something was dealt with.

examples.hanzi: 我们一起解决这个问题。
examples.english: Let's solve this problem together.
He has no solution.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 助, 男, 努: handling things takes effort. The two dots stand in for 辡 of the traditional 辦.
公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de bàngōngshì zài sān lóu.
example.english: My office is on the third floor.
example.fact: 办公室 is built from three transparent pieces stacked together — 办 ("to handle, do"), 公 ("public, official"), and 室 ("room") — literally "a room for handling official business," a [verb][domain][place-noun] pattern many three-character Mandarin nouns follow.

examples.english: He's having a meeting in the office.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ dào bàngōngshì lái yíxià.
examples.english: Please come to the office for a moment.

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 难道你忘了今天是我的生日?
example.pinyin: Nándào nǐ wàng le jīntiān shì wǒ de shēngrì?
example.english: Don’t tell me you forgot today is my birthday?
example.fact: 难道 doesn’t ask a real question — it’s a rhetorical marker that frames the speaker’s surprise or disbelief, expecting the listener to confirm what the speaker already suspects, closer in function to English "don’t tell me..." or "surely..." than to a genuine yes/no question word like 吗.

examples.english: Don't tell me you don't know?
Could it be that he doesn't want to come?

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.

example.hanzi: 作为一名老师,她非常有耐心。
example.pinyin: Zuòwéi yì míng lǎoshī, tā fēicháng yǒu nàixīn.
example.english: As a teacher, she is very patient.
example.fact: 作为 at the head of a phrase means "in the capacity of, as" (作为学生, "as a student") — a role-framing device distinct from its other, noun-like sense, "one’s conduct, actions" (他的作为让人失望, "his conduct was disappointing"), two meanings sharing one written form but doing very different grammatical jobs.

examples.pinyin: Zuòwéi péngyou, wǒ xiǎng bāng nǐ.
examples.english: As a friend, I want to help you.

examples.hanzi: 他作为学生代表发了言。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòwéi xuésheng dàibiǎo fāle yán.
examples.english: He spoke as a student representative.

components.note: 奇 (qí) is a sound clue for 骑 qí, 寄 jì, 椅 yǐ and 崎 qí; as a word it means strange or remarkable.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.

example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān de xíngwéi hěn qíguài.
example.english: His behavior today is very strange.
example.fact: 奇怪 doubles as a plain adjective ("strange, odd") and, in the first person, an expression of the speaker’s own puzzlement (我觉得奇怪, or simply 奇怪 said alone as an interjection, "how odd!") — much like English "strange" can be either a description or a muttered reaction.

examples.english: This sound is very strange.

examples.hanzi: 奇怪,我的钥匙去哪儿了?
examples.pinyin: Qíguài, wǒ de yàoshi qù nǎr le?
examples.english: Strange, where did my keys go?

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.pinyin: Tā shēng zài Shànghǎi.
example.english: He was born in Shanghai.
example.fact: 生 is one of the most versatile characters: 学生 (student), 生日 (birthday), 生活 (life), 生气 (angry), 生病 (to get sick) and 生菜 (lettuce). It means 'raw' or 'unfamiliar' as in 生字 (new character).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài Běijīng shēnghuóle wǔ nián.
examples.english: I've lived in Beijing for five years.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shēngrì shì jǐ yuè jǐ hào?
examples.english: What is your birthday?

components.note: 由 (from, reason) — mostly useful as a sound part: 油 yóu, 邮 yóu, 柚 yòu, 抽 chōu all contain it.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yóu wǒ lái zuò.
example.english: I'll take care of this.
example.fact: 由 is a formal preposition meaning 'by' or 'from': 由你决定 ('it's up to you'), 由北向南 (from north to south). It also forms 理由 (reason), 自由 (freedom) and 由于 (because of).

examples.pinyin: Zhège huì yóu jīnglǐ lái zhǔchí.
examples.english: This meeting will be chaired by the manager.
Because of the rain, the match was canceled.

components.note: 田 (field) — a field above 力 (strength): a man is one who works the fields with strength.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì nán cèsuǒ.
example.english: This is the men's restroom.
example.fact: 男 is a bound form seen in 男人 (man), 男孩 (boy), 男朋友 (boyfriend) and on restroom signs. The character shows a field (田) and strength (力), reflecting the old idea that men worked the fields.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen bān de nánshēng.
examples.english: He is a boy in our class.
Boys like playing soccer.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌: 极 first meant a roof beam, the very top.
及 (jí) gives the exact sound; also in 级 jí and 吸 xī.
子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.

example.pinyin: Zhège diànyǐng hǎokàn jí le.
example.english: This movie is extremely good.
example.fact: 极了 always follows the adjective it intensifies rather than preceding it (好看极了, never 极了好看) — the mirror image of English pre-adjective intensifiers like "extremely," and a word-order pattern shared by a small family of post-posed intensifiers including 得很 and 死了.

examples.english: It's extremely hot today!
He was extremely happy.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu tóngyì zhège jìhuà.
example.english: Everyone agrees with this plan.
example.fact: 同 contributes "same, together" and 意 contributes "opinion, intention" — 同意 reads almost transparently as "sharing the same opinion," a compositional logic clear enough that a learner who already knows both characters separately can often guess the compound’s meaning on first encounter.

examples.english: I agree with your view.
Mom doesn't agree to my going.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.

example.hanzi: 如果明天下雨，我们不去。
example.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān xiàyǔ, wǒmen bú qù.
example.english: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.
example.fact: 如 on its own is literary ('like', 'as'), but it's the core of many common words: 如果 (if), 比如 (for example), 如何 (how) and 不如 (not as good as).

examples.hanzi: 如果你有时间，请来看我。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ yǒu shíjiān, qǐng lái kàn wǒ.
examples.english: If you have time, please come see me.

examples.hanzi: 他说得如此清楚，我都听懂了。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de rúcǐ qīngchu, wǒ dōu tīngdǒng le.
examples.english: He explained so clearly that I understood it all.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and swimming, as in 河, 海, 泳: swimming and drifting.
斿 (yóu) gives the exact sound: a flag with streamers that floats freely.
戈 (halberd) — weapons, as in 战 war and 成; the traditional 戲 was a play or contest.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen lái wán yí gè yóuxì ba.
example.english: Let’s play a game.
example.fact: 游戏 covers everything from a children’s playground game to a board game to a video game (电子游戏/网络游戏) — English needs the qualifier "video" or "computer" to narrow "game" down to the digital sense, while Chinese speakers usually just say 游戏 and let context supply which kind is meant.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢玩电脑游戏。
examples.english: Kids like playing computer games.
This game is very simple.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 带, 帽: 帮 first meant the side of a shoe.
邦 (bāng, nation) gives the exact sound; 邦 itself means state or country.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 怕, 情: a heart with no rest.
亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for máng; 亡 also in 忘 wàng, 望 wàng and 盲 máng.

example.hanzi: 你能帮忙拿一下这个箱子吗?
example.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāngmáng ná yíxià zhège xiāngzi ma?
example.english: Can you help carry this box?
example.fact: 帮忙 is a verb-object compound (帮 "to help" + 忙 "a task, a favor") that generally cannot take a person as its direct object — "help someone" needs 帮 alone with the person slotted in (帮我, "help me") since 帮忙他 is not standard, the same kind of built-in object restriction seen in 结婚 (also in this batch).

examples.hanzi: 你能帮忙看一下孩子吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāngmáng kàn yíxià háizi ma?
examples.english: Can you help keep an eye on the kids?
Thanks for coming to help.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.

example.pinyin: Tā zhǐzhe dìtú shuōhuà.
example.english: He talks while pointing at the map.
example.fact: 指 is both 'finger' (手指) and the verb 'to point'. It is also used in 指的是 ('what is meant is'), 指导 (to guide) and 指南 (guide, as in a handbook).

examples.english: He points ahead with his hand.

examples.hanzi: 他手指上戴着一个戒指。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒuzhǐ shang dàizhe yí ge jièzhi.
examples.english: He is wearing a ring on his finger.

components.note: 危 (danger) — a person at the top of a cliff, with another person kneeling below: a precarious spot.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: a steep place, a risky pass.
佥 (qiān) is a loose sound clue for xiǎn; 佥 also in 检 jiǎn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 验 yàn.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, zhè tiáo lù hěn wēixiǎn.
example.english: Be careful, this road is very dangerous.
example.fact: 危 by itself is traditionally analyzed as a person crouched at the edge of a steep overhang — a vivid, almost literal image of precariousness that survives intact in the modern compound 危险, "danger."

examples.english: It's dangerous here, don't come over.
Driving too fast is dangerous.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to ask or discuss.
厂 (cliff) — the frame on the left and top, as in 原, 厚, 压. In 厌 it is just the old cliff-like frame of 厭.
犬 (quǎn, dog) — looks like a sound part but quǎn vs yàn is only a loose hint. The old 厭 got its sound from 猒 (yàn).

example.pinyin: Wǒ tǎoyàn xiàyǔ tiān.
example.english: I dislike rainy days.
example.fact: 讨厌 doubles as a verb ("to dislike, loathe") and an adjective describing an annoying person or thing (真讨厌!, "so annoying!") — in the adjective use it’s also commonly said fondly or teasingly among close friends and couples, similar to how English "you’re terrible" can be an affectionate jab rather than a real complaint.

examples.english: He really dislikes eating greens.
This mosquito is so annoying!

meanings: (past tense marker used before verb or clause)

components.note: 曾 (céng) began as a picture of a steamer (甑 zèng adds 瓦); the past-time meaning is borrowed. 曾 also gives 增 zēng, 层 céng and 赠 zèng.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.

example.hanzi: 我曾经在北京住过三年。
example.pinyin: Wǒ céngjīng zài Běijīng zhù guo sān nián.
example.english: I once lived in Beijing for three years.
example.fact: 曾经 marks a past experience that no longer holds true now — it typically pairs with the experiential aspect particle 过 on the verb (住过, "have lived [there] at some point") rather than the completion particle 了, signaling that this happened once, but that chapter is now closed.

examples.pinyin: Tā céngjīng shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: He was once my teacher.
I've been to that place before.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.
目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 眼, 睡.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for jīng; 青 also in 清, 请, 情 and 晴.

example.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjing hěn piàoliang.
example.english: Her eyes are very pretty.
example.fact: 睛 (the "eyeball" half of the compound) almost never appears on its own — outside 眼睛 and a few technical terms it's a bound morpheme that needs 眼 to form a usable word, while 眼 alone works fine by itself in compounds like 眼镜 ("glasses") and 眼泪 ("tears").

examples.english: My eyes are a bit tired.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bìshàng yǎnjing, xiǎng yi xiǎng.
examples.english: Please close your eyes and think.

meanings: outside (also pr. [wai4 mian5] for this sense)

components.note: 夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn zài xiàyǔ, nǐ yào dài sǎn.
example.english: It's raining outside, you should bring an umbrella.
example.fact: 外面 and its near-synonym 外边 both mean "outside" — paralleling the 这里/这儿 split for "here" — 外面 leans slightly more standard and written, 外边 slightly more colloquial and Beijing-flavored, though both are heard nationwide.

examples.english: He's waiting for you outside.
The world outside is big.

components.note: 夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu hěn duō xiāngtóng zhī chù.
example.english: We have many things in common.
example.fact: 处 has two readings: chù ('place, aspect', as in 好处 'benefit', 到处 'everywhere') and chǔ ('to deal with, to be in', as in 处理). Here it appears as a noun for places and aspects.

examples.pinyin: Zhège dìfang yǒu hěn duō hǎochù.
examples.english: This place has a lot of advantages.
We get along very well.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 中国是一个历史悠久的国家。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó shì yí gè lìshǐ yōujiǔ de guójiā.
example.english: China is a country with a long history.
example.fact: 国家 literally combines 国 ("state") with 家 ("family, home") — a pairing that echoes classical Confucian political thought, which often pictured the state as an extension of the family, with the ruler cast as a kind of father figure over the realm.

examples.english: I love my country.
How many countries have you been to?

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.

example.hanzi: 这个蛋糕看上去很好吃。
example.pinyin: Zhège dàngāo kàn shàng qù hěn hǎochī.
example.english: This cake looks delicious.
example.fact: 看上去 is nearly interchangeable with 看起来 — both mean "it appears, it seems" and are built the same way: verb 看 plus a directional complement (上去 "up and away" vs 起来 "up") that has faded into pure grammatical function and no longer describes literal direction.

examples.english: He looks tired.
It looks like it's going to rain.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 总 is simplified from 總, whose threads gathered everything together.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and links, as in 红, 经, 系: thread gathered into one.
充 (chōng) is only a loose sound clue for tǒng.

example.pinyin: Měiguó zǒngtǒng zhù zài Báigōng.
example.english: The US president lives in the White House.
example.fact: 总统 is reserved for the head of a republic — translating "president" as in the US or France — while China's own head of state carries the separate title 主席 ("chairman"), so 总统 essentially never refers to a Chinese leader.

examples.english: The president will give a speech today.
He wants to be president.

components.note: 门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè rén zhījiān yǒu wùhuì.
example.english: There is a misunderstanding between these two.
example.fact: 间 is also the measure word for rooms: 一间房 (a room). It is also found in 时间 (time), 空间 (space), 中间 (middle), 房间 (room) and 之间 (between).

examples.english: This room is very clean.
There are no secrets between us.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.

example.pinyin: Tā de huà shēnshēn shānghài le tā.
example.english: His words deeply hurt her.
example.fact: 伤害 is transitive — it needs an object, someone or something being harmed (伤害她, "hurt her") — while its near-relative 受伤 ("to get injured," literally "receive injury") is intransitive and describes the person harmed, a transitivity contrast that trips up many learners translating English "hurt" and "injured."

examples.pinyin: Bié shānghài nà zhī xiǎo niǎo.
examples.english: Don't hurt that little bird.

examples.hanzi: 太多的糖会伤害你的牙齿。
examples.pinyin: Tài duō de táng huì shānghài nǐ de yáchǐ.
examples.english: Too much sugar harms your teeth.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding the reins.
空 (kōng) is a close sound clue for kòng; 空 also in 腔 qiāng and 孔 kǒng.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 制 is cutting to shape, then to make and to control.

example.hanzi: 她很难控制自己的情绪。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn nán kòngzhì zìjǐ de qíngxù.
example.english: She finds it hard to control her emotions.
example.fact: 控 (built from 扌 "hand") contributes a sense of restraining or holding back, while 制 (built from 刂 "knife") contributes a sense of cutting, shaping, or regulating — together 控制 layers "restrain" onto "regulate" for its modern sense of control.

examples.english: The teacher is good at controlling the class.
The doctor got his illness under control.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is the base; the loose sound clue also appears in 趣 qù and 娶 qǔ. The top 日 here is an old cap shape, not the sun.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 远, 送: coming closer.
斤 (jīn) is a close sound clue for jìn.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zuìjìn zěnmeyàng?
example.english: How have you been recently?
example.fact: Unlike English "recently," which points only to the past, 最近 can describe the near future too (最近可能会下雨, "it may rain in the next while") — its literal meaning is just "nearest [in time]," and context decides which direction from now it points.

examples.english: I've been very busy lately.
Where is the nearest subway station?

components.note: 聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.
音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan tā shuōhuà de shēngyīn.
example.english: I like the sound of her voice.
example.fact: Like 喜欢 in the companion character-deck's pilot batch, 声音 pairs two already near-synonymous roots — 声 ("sound, voice," as in 大声 "loudly") and 音 ("sound, tone," as in 音乐 "music") — reinforcing each other into one common noun.

examples.hanzi: 我听到了一个熟悉的声音。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīngdàole yí ge shúxī de shēngyīn.
examples.english: I heard a familiar voice.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shēngyīn guān xiǎo yìdiǎn.
examples.english: Please turn the volume down a little.

components.note: 米 (rice) — grain and food, as in 粉 powder, 糕 cake, 精 refined: 糟 is dregs of fermented rice, then spoiled.
曹 (cáo) is a close sound clue for zāo; 曹 also in 遭 zāo and 槽 cáo.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān zhēn zāogāo!
example.english: Today is really terrible!
example.fact: 糟 is mostly used in 糟糕 (terrible, how awful) and 乱七八糟 (a complete mess). The original sense is the dregs of fermented grain, as in 酒糟.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de fángjiān tài zāo le.
examples.english: Your room is a mess.
Oh no, I forgot my keys!

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 怕, 忙, 情: a quick, glad heart.
夬 (guài) is a close sound clue for kuài; 夬 also in 块 kuài, 筷 kuài and 决 jué.
乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".

example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè!
example.english: Happy birthday to you!
example.fact: 快乐 tends to describe a lasting state of happiness or well-being — it's the word behind nearly every Chinese festival greeting (生日快乐 "happy birthday," 新年快乐 "happy new year") — while 高兴 describes a more momentary feeling of being pleased about something happening right now.

examples.english: Happy New Year!
The children are living happily.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 住; 偷 is a person stealing.
俞 (yú) is a loose hint for tōu; 愉 yú and 输 shū share it.

example.pinyin: Yǒu rén tōule wǒ de qiánbāo.
example.english: Someone stole my wallet.
example.fact: 偷 also means 'secretly': 偷看 (peek), 偷听 (eavesdrop) and 偷懒 (slack off). The thief is 小偷, and 偷东西 is the phrase for 'to steal things'.

examples.english: The thief stole his phone.
The child laughed secretly.

components.note: 首 (head, first) — a picture of a head with hair on top, which became the word for first and chief: 首先, 元首, also a measure for songs.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì shǒu hǎotīng de gē.
example.english: This is a nice-sounding song.
example.fact: 首 is the measure word for songs and poems (一首歌, 一首诗), and its basic meaning is 'head' or 'first': 首都 (capital), 首先 (first of all), 首次 (first time).

examples.english: This song sounds great.
He recited an ancient poem.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎomāo zhēn kě'ài.
example.english: This kitten is really cute.
example.fact: 可爱 follows a productive pattern where 可 ("able to be, worthy of") attaches to a verb to form an adjective — the same template builds 可怕 ("worthy of fear" → "scary") and 可惜 ("worthy of pity" → "a pity, unfortunately"), so spotting 可+verb is a shortcut to guessing a whole family of adjectives.

examples.english: This little kid is very cute.
She's especially lovely when she smiles.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 运动员们进入了体育场。
example.pinyin: Yùndòngyuánmen jìnrù le tǐyùchǎng.
example.english: The athletes entered the stadium.
example.fact: 进 and 入 both independently mean "to enter" — 进入 doubles up two synonymous verbs into one word, though 入 alone now reads as more literary or technical (as in 入口 "entrance," 收入 "income") while 进 alone is the everyday, spoken version.

examples.english: Everyone, please enter the classroom.

examples.hanzi: 比赛已经进入最后阶段。
examples.english: The match has entered its final stage.

components.note: 能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".
句 (jù, sentence) is a close sound clue for gòu; also in 构 gòu, 沟 gōu and 钩 gōu.
多 (many) — meaning "more than enough".

example.hanzi: 我们一定能够解决这个问题。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yídìng nénggòu jiějué zhège wèntí.
example.english: We will definitely be able to solve this problem.
example.fact: 能够 is essentially a more formal, slightly emphatic version of the plain modal verb 能 ("can, to be able to") — the two are largely interchangeable, but 能够 shows up more in writing and formal speech, while bare 能 dominates everyday conversation.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ nénggòu bāng wǒ yíxià ma?
examples.english: Can you help me for a moment?

examples.pinyin: Tā hái bù nénggòu zìjǐ zǒulù.
examples.english: He can't walk by himself yet.

components.note: 彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 事实上,他根本不知道这件事。
example.pinyin: Shìshíshàng, tā gēnběn bù zhīdào zhè jiàn shì.
example.english: In fact, he didn't know about this at all.
example.fact: 事实上 is built from 事实 ("fact," also in this batch at rank 340) plus the locative suffix 上 ("on, in terms of") — the same 上 productively turns other abstract nouns into "in terms of X" adverbials, as in 理论上 ("theoretically") and 基本上 ("basically").

examples.hanzi: 事实上,我不喜欢这个工作。
examples.pinyin: Shìshí shàng, wǒ bù xǐhuan zhège gōngzuò.
examples.english: In fact, I don't like this job.

examples.hanzi: 他看起来很年轻,事实上已经四十岁了。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlai hěn niánqīng, shìshí shàng yǐjīng sìshí suì le.
examples.english: He looks young, but he's actually forty.
